Some comments on this ceviche recipe:

1) This is reasonably authentic, unlike many ceviche recipes I have seen.
2) The author fails to mention that the type of lime matters.  Peruvian ceviche is made with what the Peruvians call "limón", which is a small, thin-skinned, juicy and very acidic lime.  The nearest fruit widely available in Canada is the key lime which is sold in many grocery stores.  Key limes cost more than regular limes but are worth it for making ceviche.
3) Sweet potato and corn are not usually mixed into the ceviche but are served on the side.
4) The marinating time is important, and should be as short as possible.  The best Peruvian ceviche is mixed and served immediately with little or no time to marinate.  The fish should not have that "cooked" appearance that it gets after sitting around in acidic lime juice for too long.  It should be as raw as sushi or sashimi is.
